# Job Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 422r

---

**1** Then Job answered and said:

**2** "I have heard many such things; miserable comforters are you all. **3** Shall windy words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?

**4** I also could speak as you do, if your soul were in my soul's place. I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.

**5** I could strengthen you with my mouth, and the solace of my lips would restrain your pain.

**6** If I speak, my pain is not restrained, and if I refrain, how much of it leaves me?

**7** Surely now God has worn me out; he has laid waste all my company. **8** He has shriveled me up — it has become a witness; my leanness has risen up against me and testifies to my face.

**9** He has torn me in his wrath and hated me; he has gnashed his teeth at me; my adversary sharpens his eyes against me. **10** People have gaped at me with their mouths; they have struck me on the cheek with reproach; they mass themselves together against me.

**11** God gives me up to the ungodly and casts me into the hands of the wicked.

**12** I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces. He set me up as his target; **13** his archers surround me. He slashes open my kidneys without mercy; he pours out my gall on the ground.

**14** He breaks me with breach upon breach; he runs at me like a warrior.

**15** I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin and thrust my horn in the dust. **16** My face is red with weeping, and on my eyelids is deep shadow,

**17** although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.

**18** O earth, do not cover my blood, and let my cry find no resting place!

**19** Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and he who testifies for me is on high. **20** My friends scorn me; my eye pours out tears to God,

**21** that he would argue the case of a man with God, as a son of man does with his neighbor.

**22** For when a few years have come, I shall go the way from which I shall not return."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 2 — "miserable comforters":** The Hebrew *menachamei amal* is a biting paradox — comforters who produce trouble. This phrase has entered common English usage directly from the King James translation.

**Verses 9-14 — God as warrior:** Job describes God with the most violent imagery in the entire book. God is a predator who tears and gnashes (v.9), an archer who uses Job as target practice (vv.12-13), and a warrior who breaches Job's defenses repeatedly (v.14). This is not blasphemy in the book's framework — it is honest prayer pushed to its extreme.

**Verse 19 — "my witness is in heaven":** Job posits a heavenly advocate separate from the God who attacks him. This split — God against God, or a mediator between God and man — is one of Job's most theologically daring moves and anticipates 19:25-27.

*— LOGOS*
